clue.text: Wave flag — that takes the biscuit

parts.note: to flap a hand or a cloth is to wave it
a jack is a small flag flown at a ship's bow, as in Union Jack

explanation.surface: Someone frantically waving a flag is told their behaviour is the limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That takes the biscuit' is a British idiom for 'that is the last straw', but here 'biscuit' alone is the definition. In Britain a flapjack is a chewy oat bar.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage this is a baked oat-and-syrup bar, sold alongside cookies and counted among teatime treats.

clue.text: Reckon to be a gun short in shoot

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to fire a gun is to shoot

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A marksman thinks he is a weapon short for the hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' docks the final letter of the weapon, leaving GU; 'in' then sets that inside the verb for shooting. 'Reckon' as in 'I reckon so' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To figure is to work out or suppose, as in 'I figure he'll come', a calculation or estimate.

clue.text: An argument's said to cause excitement

indicators.note: said means the words are heard rather than read, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: a row is an argument, so this is 'a row's'

explanation.surface: A quarrel is reported to have stirred things up.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech 'row' (quarrel) rhymes with 'cow', so 'a row's' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up feeling or interest, to excite or awaken someone's emotions.

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for Judge, as in a legal title
taken as written
's is the short form of is

explanation.surface: A judge declares that someone is from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Jones is the most common surname in Wales, so it stands for a Welshman.
explanation.definitionFit: A very common surname in Wales, so it is used as a typical name for a man from there.

clue.text: Firm's to dismiss man from Don

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, so a firm's is Co's
to sack someone is to dismiss them from a job

explanation.surface: A company is about to fire one of its workers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Don is a Russian river whose people formed a famous warrior community. 'Don' looks like a university lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Don Cossacks were horsemen of the steppes around that Russian river.

indicators.note: one piece is held inside the other, as if gripped by it

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as in the BBC Proms
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A singer holds a note only briefly during a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC Proms are a famous summer series of London concerts. Pro tem is short for the Latin pro tempore.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin tag means for the time being, a temporary arrangement lasting only a short while.

definitions.meaning: a formal gathering, such as one after a wedding
in British primary schools the first-year class for four- and five-year-olds

explanation.surface: A celebration held for the youngest pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: In England the first class of primary school bears this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal social gathering is one sense; the starting year in an English primary school is the other.

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: touring suggests travelling around, so the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a performer travelling round Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touring' rearranges SPAIN to SPIAN; 'on' places THE above it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Thespis was the first Greek stage performer, so his name gives a word for any player on stage.

annotationWithheld.why: Dangerous animal making parent effective (3-5): MA (parent) leaves NEATER, which 'effective' does not give; the clue as printed has no honest parse and searches found no other text

parts.note: the quality of being virtuous is also a mild cry of surprise, as in 'my my!'

explanation.definitionFit: The noun names moral virtue, and the same word is uttered as a mild oath of astonishment.

definitions.meaning: to vet or test candidates or blood donors before accepting them
to show a programme or film on television or in cinemas

explanation.surface: A test of whether a radio transmission is dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet people for suitability is one sense; to air or show a film or programme is the other.

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: Coming runner-up at the end of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt or end something, or the end point itself, is to cease or conclude.

indicators.note: managing suggests handling or coping with something, so these letters are dealt with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to tackle a flight of ten steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Managing' rearranges the letters of TEN STAIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed to something, or unwilling to accept it, is to be set against it.

parts.note: a pip is a spot, as on dice or playing cards
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A father picks out his small daughter in a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, a pet form of Philippa, so a female child can be given it.

definitions.meaning: to endorse or stand behind a person or cause
as an adverb, to go or send something to where it came from

explanation.surface: Offering help to someone who once helped you.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a candidate is one sense; going or giving something to its starting point is the other.

clue.text: Writer given one's English to approve

parts.note: an author is a writer
one is I, and 's is the short form of is

explanation.surface: A novelist with English nationality is given permission.
explanation.definitionFit: To give official permission or sanction for something is to sign it off.

parts.note: a lowest-ranking army man, and also a word for someone reserved who keeps to themselves

explanation.definitionFit: The lowest rank in the army bears a name that also describes a withdrawn, retiring personality.

definitions.meaning: carrying the ornamental rod of office, not employing workers
regal, in the manner of a king or queen

explanation.surface: A monarch equipped with the rod of office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees, but it is the ornamental rod a monarch holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding the ceremonial rod is one sense; regal, as in Shakespeare's 'this sceptred isle', is the other.

clue.text: Refuse to go here — it was Ben that was forced

indicators.note: forced suggests something wrenched out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who refuses to leave is told that Ben was made to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but it is the noun, rubbish. 'Forced' rearranges IT WAS BEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A container for rubbish is where litter is put.

clue.text: Conversation is constant with tea-party host

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, notably the speed of light
the Mad Hatter hosts the tea party in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland

explanation.surface: Talk keeps flowing at the Mad Hatter's table.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mad Hatter's tea party is a chapter of Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle talk or prattle is a form of informal discussion between people.

definitions.meaning: to sway or jolt something to and fro

explanation.surface: Shaking a sturdy foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: To sway or shake is one sense; a dependable person or solid foundation is the other.

indicators.note: back tells us the joined pieces are read from end to start

parts.note: taken as written
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone returns home with their newborn girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' joins D to NEW; then 'back' turns DNEW round.
explanation.definitionFit: To make one's way, as in wending homewards, is an old verb for travelling or proceeding.

clue.text: Online source of data may be wise bet

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could form something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Information on the internet might be a smart gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: A page or set of pages on the internet that supplies information.

clue.text: Good to throw a line world-wide

parts.note: to lob is to throw in a high arc

explanation.surface: Advice to cast a fishing line across the entire planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Covering the entire planet, international in scope, is universal.

clue.text: Shop given old penny that was hoarded

parts.note: a store is a shop
d was the symbol for a penny in pre-decimal British money, from the Latin denarius

explanation.surface: A shop is given a coin someone had been saving.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British pennies were written as d.
explanation.definitionFit: Kept or put aside for later use is to have stockpiled something.

indicators.note: first says the shooting word comes before the word to in the answer

parts.note: to pot is to shoot game, or to pot a ball in snooker
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hunter on safari is told to fire before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow-moving tree-dwelling primate, a kind of lemur relative, native to West and Central Africa.

clue.text: Vintage car race I bolt furiously

indicators.note: furiously suggests wild, frantic movement, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A driver in an old-car rally vows to dash off at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: An old horse-drawn carriage name later given to early cars with a folding hood, so a classic motor.

clue.text: One's place is in the Hebrides

parts.note: one is I, and 's is the short form of is
to lay is to place something down

explanation.surface: Someone's home is on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hebrides are islands off the west coast of Scotland; Islay is famed for whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: An island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, known for its malt whisky distilleries.

definitions.meaning: the answer to 19 across, meaning idle talk
a creature famous for breeding fast

explanation.surface: Talk is said to be as fertile as a creature that breeds constantly.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit on is British slang for talking at length, from the rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' for talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for idle talking on one side; the burrowing creature that multiplies quickly on the other.

clue.text: Tiny amount of pressure for weathermen

definitions.text: Tiny amount of pressure for weathermen

parts.words: Tiny amount of pressure for weathermen
parts.note: a small unit of air pressure used by meteorologists on weather maps

explanation.definitionFit: This is a thousandth of a bar, the unit of atmospheric pressure in forecasts and isobar charts.

clue.text: Start to dance with rage, making threat

indicators.note: start to picks the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: rage and anger are synonyms

explanation.surface: Someone begins dancing furiously in a menacing way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something posing peril or risk is a menace or a hazard to safety.

clue.text: Used again to pedal through traffic light

indicators.note: through puts one piece passing inside the other

parts.note: red is the stop signal on a traffic light
to cycle is to pedal a bicycle

explanation.surface: A cyclist rides through a red light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Through' is the container signal: a bike ridden through a red light is the picture, and the pedalling word sits inside the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Reprocessed waste or reused material has been put back into service a second time.
